channel.title: One Caribbean Television - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from One Caribbean Television (onecaribbeantelevision.com)

item.title: Renewed Push to Transition Puerto Rico from NAP to SNAP Benefits
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Puerto Rico’s Governor and a handful of Senate Democrats said the territory’s residents have been treated differently when it comes to receiving federal food benefits. There’s a renwed effort in Congress to get SNAP benefits for Puerto Ricans.

item.title: USVI LEPC Cleared of Federal “High-risk” Status After More Than a Decade of Oversight, Gov. Bryan Weighs In
item.description: The Virgin Islands Law Enforcement Planning Commission (LEPC) is no longer considered “high-risk” by the U.S. Department of Justice, ending a period of heightened oversight that began in 2012. The designation stemmed from concerns raised by federal investigators about grant management tied to events over a decade ago.

item.title: Gov. Bryan Looking Forward to FEMA Assistance, Nearly $28 Million Will Aid Hurricane Recovery Projects in USVI
item.description: The Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) recently approved nearly $28 million in disaster recovery funding for the U.S. Virgin Islands to help repair damage caused by Hurricane Maria.

item.title: Expert: Iran’s New Supreme Leader Sends “Political Statement” to US, Israel and Iranians
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Motjaba Khamenei, the son of Iran’s former Supreme Leader, Ali Khamenei, who was killed in the US-Israeli strikes, has been named as the new Supreme Leader. Experts said it’s a political statement to the US, Israel and Iranians who thought there could be a shift in leadership.

item.title: Trump Administration Gives Mixed Signals on Timeline for Iran Operations
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - As Congressional Democrats air their concerns about a prolonged war in Iran, Secretary Pete Hegseth said Tuesday will be the most intense strikes on Iran.

item.title: Leaders Try to Balance U.S. Dominance in A.I. and Energy Costs for Data Centers
item.description: The artificial intelligence (AI) boom is driving a surge in new data centers across the country — but the massive power demand is sparking debate in communities about energy costs and infrastructure.

item.title: Democratic Senator, Governors Want Tariff Refunds and Relief
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - In late February, the Supreme Court struck down the President’s use of emergency powers to issue tariffs. Soon after the ruling, Trump said he would use a different route to implement tariffs. A handful of Democratic governors and a US Senator are looking to rein in the President’s tariffs.

item.title: SAVE America Act Faces Uncertain Future in Senate, Trump Demands Action Ahead of 2026 Midterms
item.description: The SAVE America Act would require proof of citizenship to register to vote — and photo ID to cast a ballot, even though it is already illegal for noncitizens to vote in federal elections. Supporters say the measure protects the integrity of American elections, but critics warn it could create new barriers for millions of voters.

item.title: Iran Conflict Creates “Largest Supply Disruption” in History of Global Oil Market
item.description: WASHINGTON, D.C. - Oil prices jumped even after the US and an international organization announced emergency reserves would be released. The price of oil and gas has been volatile since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran.

item.title: A Message, Supposedly from New Supreme Leader, Vows Retribution as Iranian President Shares Demands for End to War
item.description: A purported message from Iran’s new supreme leader comes as “Operation Epic Fury” approaches its third week. What is believed to be the new voice at the top of Iran’s power structure is promising retribution as the conflict between Iran, Israel and the U.S. intensifies.
